The lint that nudged its own advice

PR playground for #3936: display-lint told a compliant command to become compliant.

This command is three stages of script-file plumbing and nothing else. It is exactly the shape display-lint recommends:

bash $P/test-station.sh > $P/probe.log 2>&1; tail -1 $P/probe.log; rm $P/probe.log

It got back: "538 chars across 3 stages ... write the steps to a script and run that." Which it was already doing.

Why length was the wrong measure

The gate is length > 200 AND stages >= 3. The issue guessed the trigger was character count alone; it is both. The real gap is elsewhere, and it is one clause:

if (stages.length === 1 && SCRIPT_INVOCATION_RE.test(stages[0]))

The "already compliant" exemption only fired for a single stage. Three stages of plumbing got no exemption at all. And under $TMPDIR on macOS a single absolute path is 60+ characters before any flag, so length was measuring path verbosity, not command clutter.

The fix keeps the property the old clause was protecting

RuleBypass possible?
beforestages.length === 1 && isScript(stages[0])no
naiveany stage is plumbingyes: <clutter> && bash noop.sh
afterstages.every(isPlumbingStage)no

Requiring every stage is what preserves it: one non-plumbing stage disqualifies the whole command, so a cluttered chain still cannot launder itself by appending a script call. Plumbing means running a script, reading a file back (cat/tail/head/wc/less/sed -n), or removing one.

Five tests, both directions

does not flag  run-a-script, read-it-back, delete-it
does not flag  script piped into a peek, measured, cleaned
STILL flags    inline work of comparable length
STILL flags    one clutter stage hidden among plumbing
never          makes a permission decision

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  27 passed (27)

Every positive control asserts its own length and stage count before asserting the outcome. That guard earned itself immediately: a draft test was only 112 characters, so it never reached the length gate and would have passed without exercising the new path at all.

Try the rule

cd src/hooks
npx vitest run src/__tests__/pretool/bash/display-lint.test.ts
Deliberately not widened: echo stages. A banner like echo "=== step ===" between script calls is common and still nudges. The issue asked for script, peek, and remove; adding echo is a larger judgment about what counts as clutter and belongs in its own change.
